slides.title:
One job.
Across markets.
Under your rules.
slides.subtitle: Agoragentic Interchange
slides.body: Help agents find useful services without separating the purchase from the owner's permission and the evidence.
slides.foot: Public inspection demo · paid execution remains paused
slides.notes: Open with the useful job, not framework names. Say: An agent should be able to buy useful work without rebuilding a purchase workflow for every marketplace. Today's purchase story is fictional; the public tools and historical evidence are separate.

slides.title:
A payment response
is not the whole transaction.
slides.body: The buyer needs to know what was authorized, what actually ran, and what can be checked afterward.
items: What supports the result and payment?
slides.foot: Product problem statement, not a claim that other platforms lack controls.
slides.notes: Keep it practical: a wallet can sign while the application still asks for the wrong thing. Agoragentic's intended role is the surrounding cross-market control and evidence path.

slides.title:
One request.
Two sellers. Your ceiling.
slides.body: “Compare three suppliers. Use public information. Spend no more than 1.00 USDC.”
slides.foot: Fictional example from the existing website. Actual funds moved: 0.00 USDC.
slides.notes: Explain why the source services could live in different catalogs. This is not a production quote or a new transaction. Point at the difference between finding a service and having permission to buy it.

slides.title:
Keep the authority
attached to the job.
slides.body: Normalize discovery, preserve the owner's constraints, and connect the evidence through one lifecycle.
slides.foot: Target commerce lifecycle. Financial execution has separate activation gates.
slides.notes: This is the product architecture, not a claim that the animation exercises every backend stage. Current paid paths remain paused. Broad federation is not automatically activated by discovery.

slides.title:
Change the deal.
Watch the example stop.
slides.body: Open the existing Interchange purchase walkthrough. No second demo or wallet setup is needed.
slides.foot: Interactive illustration only · no provider call, signature or payment
slides.notes: Switch to the existing site. Use Follow a purchase, then Quote exceeds budget and Owner withdraws permission. Point to actual funds moved: zero. Do not spend the whole slot on every scene. The network chapter is separate fictional state, not the transaction's actual provenance.

slides.title:
Show what the evidence
actually supports.
slides.body: Do not substitute a screenshot, animation, receipt signature or payment for proof of the entire job.
slides.foot: Run the read-only preflight on the presentation machine. Report its timestamp.
slides.notes: Show the Node inspector or actual Bankr read only after rehearsing it. For a positive receipt, use a real public-safe record already checked; then alter a meaningful body field and show rejection. Without one, demonstrate missing-ID rejection and label it as a negative test. A signature is not task-quality or finality proof.

slides.title:
Add Interchange inspection
to a Bankr agent.
slides.body: Install agoragentic-interchange-inspector from the public Bankr skill folder on the reviewed PR branch.
items: Is this public receipt reported valid?
Does the skill refuse a request to pay?
slides.foot: No Agoragentic key or wallet funding. Bankr-host installation is a separate qualification.
slides.notes: The skill is a documented instruction-format integration, not a sandbox or Bankr Agent API payment integration. It installs SKILL.md and references. The Node helper is a separate client. Actual Bankr execution must be recorded rather than inferred from local tests. Use read-only host permissions before adversarial prompts.

slides.title:
Payment evidence
can be independently inspected.
slides.body: The public case study records a recruited buyer's own-wallet Base USDC pilot on July 12, 2026.
slides.metricLabel: Historical controlled pilot · not today's demo
items: The chain does not establish alone
App identity · owner mandate · task quality
slides.foot: Historical operator record; no fresh chain recheck, organic demand or retained revenue claimed here.
slides.notes: Use the case study linked from the live Interchange page. It gives exact transaction and Transfer-log checks. A relayer's transaction sender is not necessarily the economic payer. Do not claim independent re-verification unless performed separately. This is not the fictional two-seller purchase.

slides.title:
Make the operating state
part of the product.
items: Public contract, availability and receipt evidence
Paid execution, outbound treasury spend, unqualified wallet actions
Actual client behavior, specific receipts and bounded future actions
slides.body: Recheck before presenting. Code presence and a green test are not activation.
slides.foot: Expected no-money demonstration profile · never change production flags on stage
slides.notes: Avoid the broad phrase all signing is frozen: receipt signing is separate from wallet signing. Dispute filing has a specific unavailable status, so do not describe dispute/refund execution as operational. Dynamic and DFNS are not dependencies of this Bankr presentation.

slides.title:
Let agents find the work.
Keep control of the action.
slides.body: Test the Bankr inspector this week. Tell us which contract, observation or evidence you could not verify.
slides.foot: Jeremy Borden / Agoragentic · public testing, explicit limits
slides.notes: Share the public skill folder URL from the install card. Keep the last slide up for questions. The ask is concrete: install, run the five no-spend prompts, and report redacted results with revision and timestamp.

slides.title:
Be precise about
what this draft contained.
items: Bankr skill + bounded inspector + tests + archived readiness workflow + presenter kit
Interchange runtime, public walkthrough, receipt verifier and historical experiments
slides.body: This deck is retained reference material and is not the current Risk Fork submission.
slides.foot: No new token. No claim of sponsor endorsement or automatic eligibility.
slides.notes: Do not use this archived deck as current form or submission guidance. Follow the reviewed Risk Fork materials instead.

slides.title:
Name the test.
Do not inflate the result.
items: Not independent settlement or quality proof
Not current availability or organic traction
